GLP-1, or glucagon-like peptide-1, is a naturally occurring hormone in the body that regulates blood sugar, appetite, and digestion [web3]. It is a peptide hormone derived from tissue-specific posttranslational processing of the proglucagon peptide [web2].

GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are a class of medications that mimic the effects of this natural hormone [web3]. GLP-1RAs have demonstrated several potential therapeutic effects, including limiting the development of atherosclerotic plaques through anti-inflammatory mechanisms and preventing vascular remodeling [doc1]. They also exhibit anti-adhesive and anti-thrombotic properties in the endothelium, potentially delaying atherosclerosis [doc1].

GLP-1RAs are primarily used to manage blood sugar levels in people with Type 2 diabetes and can also help treat obesity [web1, web4]. Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, and abdominal pain [web3].

**Please note:** GLP-1 drugs are prescription medications and should only be taken under the supervision of a healthcare professional [web3].
